## Retained baseline and scope

Baseline: `714b4440b81cdcabdab2ed8376289e24be15682c` (2026-11-03). Previously verified: 42 suites, headless memory checks, hardware/software rendered workflows and older saves. This planning update does not rerun or upgrade that evidence.

- C++/Vulkan engine and software fallback
- 100,000-person/2,000-floor configurable world and three modes
- Ownership, economy, physical jobs, queues, construction, transport and core NPC routines
- Households/storage, companies/equity, estates, investigations and medical/death systems
- Bounded connected-floor fire/smoke/cargo loss, multilingual UI, saved controls and procedural sound

Accepted design: [docs/requirements.md](requirements.md). Historical implementation evidence: [docs/status.md](status.md). Older status entries do not select the next task.

Platform target: Complete Linux and Windows player packages; support claims require actual platform validation.

**Cancelled scope; do not reintroduce:**

- Floating island / explorable outside city / separate outside hospital
- Creative mode (superseded by Survival, Manager and Cheat)

| Phase | Milestones | Exit goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0: Scope and baseline | [M00](#m00) | Establish the finite acceptance register once; retain all existing work. |
| P1: Resident autonomy and daily life | [M01–M03](#m01) | Finish independent social, household and financial behaviour. |
| P2: Flexible construction and property | [M04–M07](#m04) | Complete live building changes, displacement and structural consequences. |
| P3: Vehicles and physical interactions | [M08–M11](#m08) | Complete contact physics, traffic and transport ownership. |
| P4: Companies, work, schooling and inheritance | [M12–M17](#m12) | Make careers, businesses and generational assets function as complete loops. |
| P5: Crime, medicine and disasters | [M18–M21](#m18) | Complete physical enforcement, care and emergency consequences. |
| P6: World presentation, animation, UI and sound | [M22–M27](#m22) | Bring the usable systems to the requested visual and interaction standard. |
| P7: Compatibility, GPU scaling, balance and release | [M28–M32](#m28) | Verify the complete game and produce supported player-ready builds. |

Gameplay comes first. Performance work is P7; an earlier correctness or responsiveness fix stays attached to the milestone it unblocks.

## Rules for continuing work

- Read this tracker and completion-plan.md on every implementation continuation; resume the current task rather than choosing a new theme.
- Execute milestone IDs in order. Finish and verify the current milestone before starting the next; do not restart already delivered baseline systems.
- Work on one milestone at a time. A prerequisite bug fix belongs to that milestone; record what it unblocks and return immediately to the current task.
- Acknowledge a user priority/scope change with a dated change_log entry; do not silently reorder, add release blockers or replace the accepted design.
- New optional ideas go to future_ideas, not the release backlog. A required connecting task goes under its existing owner milestone with a reason.
- Keep each accepted feature coherent across rules, actual movement/actions, NPC choice, player interaction, ownership/economy, interruption/death, saves, localization and presentation.
- Complete a task only with relevant evidence; complete a milestone only when all its tasks and acceptance criteria pass. Test counts alone never prove feature or game completion.
- Use appropriate focused/regression checks and real rendered play; broaden/repeat only after relevant changes, failures or unresolved concerns. Do not rerun the entire native suite for plan-only edits.
- Preserve player saves and the old browser prototype. Verify/install/publish working code checkpoints using the already authorized project workflow.
- Before ending an implementation turn, update task status, evidence, blocker/next action and next task pointer; report completed IDs and the exact next ID. Do not ask what to do next when this plan already answers it.
- Only M32 passing its complete release gate permits an overall finished/shippable claim. An individual code checkpoint or portable archive remains a development update until then.

## Completion criteria for every milestone

- Rules and required edge/failure cases behave as specified; no decorative-only substitute for a required action.
- Player and NPC actors use real movement, staffing, tools, resources, ownership, payments and permissions.
- Interruption, cancellation, competing claims, surrender, death, emigration and changed availability retain valid state.
- Persistent state round-trips and required older/browser fixtures continue without lost or duplicated resources.
- English, French and Chinese names/text/input remain coherent; required UI and animation/feedback are usable.
- Relevant invariant, regression, CPU/GPU and memory checks pass; appropriate rendered and manual play evidence is recorded.
- Limits and remaining work are attributed to another numbered milestone or an explicit future idea, never silently declared complete.

Every completed task needs evidence in its `evidence` list. A completed milestone also needs a date, an overall evidence record and one `acceptance_evidence` entry per criterion below. When tasks are finished but acceptance is under review, keep the milestone active with a null current task. Advance the pointer only after the gate passes. M00 is a one-time inventory, not a recurring restart.

### M17 — Property valuation, succession and contested estates

**Status:** pending · **Depends on:** M16 · **Phase:** P4

**Tasks**

- [ ] **M17.2** Finish personal/corporate succession, dependents, contested nominations, creditor priority and unclaimed-property liquidation.

**Gate — all must pass**

1. Adding/removing nearby services changes measured property value for understandable reasons without invalidating leases.
2. Death/succession distributes each actual asset, claim and debt once; late money reaches the right heir or outside economy.
3. The owner is not always for sale; every ownership route has actual actors, resources and consequences.

### M29 — GPU parallel simulation and streamed world scaling

**Status:** pending · **Depends on:** M28 · **Phase:** P7

**Tasks**

- [ ] **M29.1** Profile the completed game on the recorded reference GPU and CPU fallback before choosing expensive work to offload.
- [ ] **M29.2** Implement streamed/cached geometry/textures, crowd/detail LOD and GPU animation sampling where it improves actual play.
- [ ] **M29.3** Offload suitable resident/crowd/needs or other large parallel work with explicit CPU reference checks and safe synchronization.
- [ ] **M29.4** Meet the documented default-world frame, responsiveness, memory and simulation-progress budgets without deleting features.

**Gate — all must pass**

1. The 100,000-resident/2,000-floor world keeps up at 1× compressed time with bounded processing backlog and responsive controls.
2. Reference GPU target: 1080p/60 FPS target, p95 frame time at most 33 ms and p99 at most 50 ms in the recorded dense-play route; ordinary UI responses at most 100 ms.
3. The recorded CPU-only 720p preset targets at least 15 FPS and usable controls; CPU/GPU paths preserve the same validated rules, ownership and accounting.

**Requirement coverage:** R02, R04, R32, R33, R34, R35, R38

## Required whole-game release scenarios

- Survival: configurable new game → move in → queue and meet needs → actual paid work → device purchase → real delivery → better housing → vehicle/business asset → ownership opportunity or refusal.
- Manager: actual budget/staffing → planned funded construction → compensation or contested eviction → working profitable facility → emergency response/repair → succession or move-out game over.
- Cheat: roleplay and inspect/possess residents → bounded edits to all supported rules/entities → coherent world, accounting and saves.
- Conflict: queue cut/theft → witnesses/report → physical combat/surrender → evidence-based enforcement → cell/escape/rescue → actual release/recovered property.
- Disaster: disease/fire/structural damage → warning/evacuation → staffed paid response → treatment/death/body handling → estate/claims → funded physical recovery.
- Continuity: old native/browser import → preserve identities/titles/prepaid work/families → play each relevant system → save in another named slot → reload/recover after a corrupt primary.
